messages:
nina: Hey benefits 14 quick one14 had a mole removed at Shoreline Dermatology last month. Clinic said it was in-network, but I just got an EOB showing the lab and procedure billed as out-of-network. Claim#: 987654321. They billed under "Shoreline Surgical Associates" TIN instead of the clinic's TIN. Anyone seen this type of billing name mismatch?

sam_people_ops: Yep, billing entity vs facility name mismatches are pretty common. It can cause auto-deny if the insurer's contracted TIN doesn't match the billed TIN. Did the clinic give you any paperwork showing they operate under the same TIN?

nina: I have the itemized bill that lists both the dermatologist name and the billing entity as Shoreline Surgical Associates (wrong TIN). The clinic front desk told me it's the pathology lab that bills separately.

olivia-benefits: Two parallel fixes: 1) Ask the clinic to submit a corrected claim/void+rebill with the clinic's contracted TIN and NPI. 2) Ask the insurer for a reprocessing request referencing the patient's original member ID + claim#. Broker can also confirm whether pathology should be bundled or separate.

billing-clinic: Hi Nina 12 this is Shoreline Billing. Sorry for the confusion 12 the pathology is subcontracted and bills under Shoreline Surgical Associates TIN. We can request that pathology append the rendering dermatologist's NPI and resubmit. If you want, we can initiate the corrected claim today.

broker-julia: I'll open a network ops ticket with Acme and request reprocessing for claim 987654321 once the clinic files a corrected claim. If Acme rejects on TIN mismatch, request they consider the rendering NPI + facility relationship as proof to process in-network.

insurance-bot: Support case created: ACME-CLAIM-202606-5533. Status: awaiting corrected claim from provider.

ben-hr: For the employee note: if the claim denial results in a patient balance, we can temporarily front the cost via our benefits exceptions fund pending final reprocessing. Not ideal but it's an option if the clinic can't get it fixed quickly. Nina, do you need short-term assistance?

nina: I might need help if it doesn't reprocess. Current EOB shows patient responsibility $1,420. Oof. Would prefer to get claim fixed first.

billing-clinic: We submitted a corrected claim this morning and attached the pathology report linking the rendering doc's NPI. Reference: correction SR# 1229. We'll follow up with Acme to confirm receipt.

broker-julia: Acme updated ACME-CLAIM-202606-5533: corrected claim received; pending adjudication. Estimated turnaround 7-10 business days. I've requested expedited review because the lab was subcontracted and documentation shows clinical relationship.

insurance-bot: ACME-CLAIM-202606-5533 updated: adjudication in progress.

olivia-benefits: Filing internal note: "Claim 987654321 initially denied for TIN mismatch; provider resubmitted corrected claim; broker requested expedited re-adjudication. Employee advised on short-term fund option if needed."

nina: Thank you all 12 keeping fingers crossed. If anything changes, I'll post the final EOB here so we can close the loop. :crossed_fingers:

insurance-bot: ACME-CLAIM-202606-5533 closed: claim reprocessed at in-network rates; patient responsibility adjusted to $45 copay. Notification emailed to member.

ben-hr: Great outcome. Marking as closed in tracker and removing provisional exception. Nina 12 glad that worked out! :tada:
